items.title: Processional Cross
items.summary: La Croce Processionale, realizzata dal Maestro di Santa Chiara (Italia) intorno al 1320, era originariamente destinata a essere portata in processione religiosa. Le figure rappresentano Cristo crocifisso e la Vergine Maria con San Giovanni Battista, esprimendo intensa tristezza.
items.titleIt: Croce Processionale - Cleveland Museum of Art
items.excerpt: Processional Cross. Master of Santa Chiara (Italian). c. 1320. oil on canvas on wood. Italy, Umbria. This cross was originally mounted on a tall pole and carried in religious processions. Therefore, the figures on each side are almost identical. In the center is Christ crucified.

quiz.q: ¿Qué santos están representados en los terminales inferiores de la cruz?
options: San Juan Bautista y el Apóstol Mateo.

items.title: Machinist's Apprentice

items.titleIt: Apprendista Meccanico
items.excerpt: Machinist's Apprentice. Emma Stebbins (American, 1815–1882). c. 1859. Marble. Stebbins belonged to a community of women sculptors in Rome. Like their male colleagues, they sought to emulate the statues of antiquity. In a rare pair of marble statues, Stebbins portrays a machinist and his apprentice, an unusual theme in mid-19th-century American sculpture.

quiz.q: Quale soggetto insolito viene raffigurato nella scultura di Emma Stebbins?
options: Un meccanico e il suo apprendista

THEY should never have built a barn there, at all--
Drip, drip, drip!--under that elm tree,
Though then it was young. Now it is old
But good, not like the barn and me.
To-morrow they cut it down. They will leave
The barn, as I shall be left, maybe.
What holds it up? 'Twould not pay to pull down.
Well, this place has no other antiquity.
No abbey or castle looks so old
